title: MCDX: Model Capability Differential Explorer — automated comparator and market tracker
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build an automated, queryable comparator (Model Capability Differential Explorer, MCDX) that ingests model specs, benchmark signals, feature flags, and vendor telemetry to surface the smallest meaningful capability deltas that matter for Redwood customers. Goal: reduce manual triage time for PMs/SEs by 70% when evaluating new or updated open models, and produce daily signals for the model-watchlist pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline ingests model metadata from 3 sources (HF model zoo, vendor release notes, internal evals) on a daily cadence
Web UI / query endpoint returns a ranked differential report between any two models within 30s
Automated alerting rules generate top-10 capability deltas for the watchlist and push to Slack channel #model-watchers
Reports include actionable migration guidance: quantization compatibility risk, hardware affinity, expected latency delta (p50) and estimated token-cost delta
Initial launch supports text-generation and embeddings model types, with clear extension points for multimodal
deliverables: Ingestion pipeline (Airflow task + adapters) for HF, vendor RSS, internal eval exports
Canonical MCDX schema and small-document store (searchable) for model feature vectors
Comparator service (HTTP API) with diff ranking and scoring heuristics
Lightweight web UI prototype with comparator inputs and visualization
Operational runbook and daily signal Slack integration
architecture_notes: MCDX will store normalized feature vectors (stringified JSON blobs stored in a document DB). Comparator uses a weighted-difference scoring: capability match, SAFETY/regressions, latency/cost taxonomy. Start lightweight: use existing ETL infra (Airflow + S3 staging) and a single EC2 for prototype comparator. Plan migration to dedicated microservice and Dynamo-like store in Q2 if adoption metrics justify.
